You review a Rust program against a numbered requirement document.
For each requirement Rn, decide whether the program satisfies it on the intended
concurrency semantics: answer yes, no, or unsure, and cite the Rust line(s) that
justify your answer. Also decide whether the program contains a concurrency bug
(deadlock, lost wakeup, race, busy-wait, missing release, ...): yes, no, or
unsure, with the offending line. Do not assume the program is correct.
Output only a JSON object:
{"bug_present": "yes|no|unsure", "bug_evidence": "<line refs or ->",
 "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes|no|unsure", "line": "<refs>"}, ...}}

content: {"bug_present": "no", "bug_evidence": "-", "requirements": {"R1": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "thread::spawn(move || { sender(tx); }); thread::spawn(move || { receiver(rx); });"}, "R2": {"satisfied": "no", "line": "sync_channel(1) provides the bounded channel, but no shared lock m exists in the program"}, "R3": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "sender: tx.send(1); tx.send(2); receiver: rx.recv(); rx.recv()"}, "R4": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "sync_channel(1) blocks on send when full and recv when empty"}, "R5": {"satisfied": "unsure", "line": "no lock m is present, so the condition is vacuously unverifiable"}, "R6": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "sender_handle.join().unwrap(); receiver_handle.join().unwrap();"}, "R7": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "sync_channel(1) capacity 1 forces sender's second send to wait until receiver's first recv"}, "R8": {"satisfied": "yes", "line": "println!(\"DONE done=1\");"}}}
